title: Two-Sided System Incidence Candidate V1
motivation: 2014 Stock Connect broker shadow succeeded while 2013 IPO-restart broker selection failed despite both having mechanical broker revenue links.
purpose: Before allowing a pre-report market-structure selection, explicitly map both the direct company revenue/capital benefit and any simultaneous system-level offset that changes market liquidity, asset supply, funding, risk appetite or benchmark opportunity cost.

dimensions.name: direct_company_incidence
dimensions.question: What quantity changes mechanically for the company: transaction volume, underwriting volume, funding cost, balance-sheet capacity, market share, fee pool?

dimensions.name: system_liquidity_incidence
dimensions.question: Does the same event add or remove secondary-market liquidity, increase asset supply, tighten funding, or change risk appetite?

dimensions.name: cross_sectional_purity
dimensions.question: Is the company disproportionately exposed to the positive side relative to controls, or is it mostly market beta?

dimensions.name: timing_asymmetry
dimensions.question: Does the benefit arrive before the system offset, after it, or simultaneously?

dimensions.name: benchmark_opportunity_cost
dimensions.question: Could a positive absolute company outcome still be inferior to the broader market regime?

rules: This is a research dimension only; no hard gate or score is adopted.
Do not reinterpret 2013 or 2014 labels after outcome.
A mechanical company benefit is not sufficient if the same event has a plausible offsetting system effect.
No production change before an untouched replication.
